transcript.content: Hello, welcome. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

Well… I guess I’m here because my thinking hasn’t been as sharp lately. It’s probably not a huge thing, but at work I’ll be looking at a board packet or a vendor email, things I used to get through pretty quickly, and my head just feels cloudy. I’ll sit there and have trouble deciding even simple things. I’m not sure if that’s the right way to explain it.
Can you describe what happens when you're trying to read or make decisions at work? Do you find yourself getting distracted easily, or does it feel more like your thinking is slowed down overall?

It’s more like everything slows down, I think. I mean, I might glance away here and there, but the main thing is I’ll be staring at a board packet or an email from a vendor and it just doesn’t click the way it used to. Even little decisions feel harder, like I should be able to answer quickly and I just… sit there. It’s not terrible all the time, but it’s noticeable enough that I thought I should mention it.
Have you noticed any changes in your mood lately, like feeling down, sad, or losing interest in things you usually enjoy?

A little, yes. I don’t want to make it sound too dramatic, but I haven’t really felt like doing some of the things I usually like. Like my dance class… I’ve been skipping that, and I haven’t wanted to go look at the little galleries like I normally do. Even cooking Sunday food for my family, which usually makes me feel like myself, has felt like too much. Is that the kind of thing you mean?
Have you had trouble concentrating on tasks, even ones that you used to find easy, or do you feel like your thoughts are foggy most days?

Yes… I think “foggy” is a good word for it. It’s not like I can’t do anything, but my head feels cloudy, especially with things I used to handle pretty fast. I’ll stare at a board packet or a vendor email and just sort of get stuck, even on a simple decision. I know that probably sounds small, but it’s been happening enough that I noticed it.
Have you noticed that you're feeling more tired or that you're lacking energy to do things, even things that wouldn't usually bother you?

I’m not sure I’d say I’m more tired, exactly. I mean, I’m 64, so I don’t want to make too much of normal things, you know? I haven’t really noticed a big change in my energy. Some things feel like more effort, but I don’t know if that’s tiredness or just… having a harder time getting going. Does that answer it okay?
Have you been feeling down or having a low mood most of the day, nearly every day, lately?

I don’t think it’s most of the day, nearly every day… at least I wouldn’t want to say that if I’m not sure. I have had some low moments, but I’m still getting through things. Maybe more “not quite myself” than deeply down, if that makes sense. Is that the kind of distinction you’re asking about?
Can you tell me if there have been days when you’ve felt down or low for most of the time, and if so, how often that happens?

I’m not sure I can say it happens for most of the day, no. I mean, I have some days where I feel lower or kind of discouraged, but it usually comes and goes. I haven’t really kept count, honestly. I don’t want to overstate it. Maybe there are stretches in a day where I’m down, but “most of the time” feels like… I’m not sure. Is that helpful?
Have you noticed that you don’t take as much pleasure in things you used to enjoy, or that you don’t really care about them the way you used to?

A little, yes… I don’t want to make it sound worse than it is, but I have noticed I haven’t really wanted to go to my dance class, or look around the little galleries like I usually do. And even cooking Sunday food for my family, which normally makes me feel like myself, feels like something I’m just not drawn to right now. I still care, I think… it’s just not giving me that same feeling. Does that make sense?
Over the past few weeks, have you had several days in a row where you felt down or low for most of the day, nearly every hour?

I’m not sure I’d say several days in a row like that, no. I’ve had low spells, but when you say “most of the day, nearly every hour,” that feels a little stronger than what I can honestly say. I don’t want to answer it wrong, but I haven’t really noticed it being that constant.
Looking back over the last few weeks, have you had a period of time where you felt down or low nearly every hour of the day, and if so, how long did that last?

I don’t think I’d say it was nearly every hour of the day, exactly… but the down stretches have been sort of coming and going for maybe about a year now. This latest one, though, it feels more connected to things after my husband stopped working. I hope that answers what you’re asking.
Can you tell me if there has been a time in the last few months when you felt down or low every day, or nearly every day, for most of the day, and if so, how long that lasted?

I’m trying to think how to say it right… I don’t know if I can honestly say it was every day, most of the day, for one solid stretch. It’s more like these low patches have been coming back on and off for maybe about a year. This latest one feels more connected to what happened after my husband stopped working, if that makes sense.
Can you tell me if there has been a period in the last few months when you felt down or low for most of the day, nearly every day, and if so, how long that lasted?

I guess… I’m not sure I’d call it one clear period where it was most of the day nearly every day. It’s more that these depressed stretches keep coming back off and on, maybe for about a year now. This latest one feels more tied to what happened after my husband stopped working. Does that make sense?
Can you tell me if there has been a two-week period in the last few months when you felt down or low for most of the day, nearly every day?

Yes… I think so. I don’t want to make it sound worse than it is, but this sharper change—with my energy and confidence, and then that low, cloudy feeling—has been going on about two weeks now, since my husband retired and was suddenly home all day. Does that answer it okay?
Have you noticed any changes in your appetite or weight recently—like eating less than usual or losing or gaining a noticeable amount of weight?

A little, yes… I mean, I haven’t really been keeping track of my weight, so I don’t want to overstate it. But my eating has been off. Some days coffee and just a few bites of something will carry me through most of the day, and then at night I’ll kind of pick at tortillas or something sweet, not really enjoying it. Is that the kind of thing you mean?

Have you noticed that you’ve lost interest in activities you usually enjoy, like your dance class or cooking for your family, or do you still find some pleasure in them even if it feels a bit different lately?

Yes… I still can enjoy things a little once in a while, I think, but lately I just haven’t wanted to do the things I normally like. Like my dance class—I keep not going. And I haven’t felt like looking at the little galleries or cooking Sunday food for my family, and those are usually the things that make me feel like myself. I don’t know if that counts as losing interest, but it feels different.
